correctness.rationale: All quantifiers p>1, finite positive measure, nonzero atomless part, x unit, t>=0 are covered. A gliding-hump argument proves uniform atomic-coordinate tightness of a weak-null ℓ1-sum sequence; coordinatewise ℓp splitting and a 2D Minkowski inequality give atomic lower bound (a^p+s^p)^(1/p). The diffuse two-sided triangle inequality gives max(b,t-s). Minimizing over s in [0,t] gives the displayed exact piecewise profile. Explicit atom-coordinate e_n and nonatomic Rademacher sign sequences achieve the bound with norm t. Boundary a=0,b=0,t=0,t=b and arbitrary countably many atoms were checked. This is an analytic proof; numerical illustrations are not certificates.

value.rationale: This gives a complete pointwise weak-null perturbation norm profile for all t>=0 and 1<p<infinity for any finite mixed atomic/nonatomic measure, explaining quantitatively why the atomless WASQ theorem ceases to hold exactly at positive atomic mass. The factor 2^(1/p)-1 depends on genuinely infinite-dimensional fiber geometry rather than a scalar routine substitution, and the sharp piecewise phase threshold t=b is a natural invariant of the nonatomic mass. Explicit optimal witnesses and lower-bound rigidity make the answer reusable for quantitative Banach-space geometry; no speculative application is needed.
